notes.meaning: Jacob and his family moved into Egypt to survive a severe famine. The name "land of Ham" refers to Egypt, named after Noah's son Ham whose descendants settled there. Jacob lived there as a visiting stranger rather than a permanent citizen, trusting that God would one day bring his family home.

While living in Egypt, the family of Israel grew rapidly into a vast nation. God blessed them so richly that they soon outnumbered the local Egyptians. Even when trials came, the Lord kept His ancient promise to multiply Abraham's descendants.

As Israel grew strong, the Egyptian rulers became fearful and turned against them with cruel plots. God used this rising hostility as part of His greater plan to rescue His people from bondage. What human beings planned for evil, the Lord directed to bring about their deliverance.

differ.view: God actively and sovereignly directed the minds of the Egyptians to fulfill His purposes, while the Egyptians remained fully guilty for their own hatred.
God did not put evil into human hearts, but pulled back His restraining Spirit and allowed the Egyptians' natural jealousy to take over as Israel prospered.

notes.meaning: God chose Moses and his brother Aaron to lead the people out of slavery. Neither man took this heavy duty upon himself; the Lord called them and equipped them to speak on His behalf. They were sent as faithful servants to confront the king of Egypt.

Moses and Aaron announced the Lord's warnings and performed miraculous signs throughout Egypt. These wonders were visible proofs of God's supreme power over the land. Each sign showed that the God of Israel was far greater than Pharaoh and his gods.

God covered the land with a deep, terrifying darkness that shut out all sunlight. Even under this overwhelming display of divine power, Pharaoh and his leaders stubbornly refused to listen to God's word. Their defiance brought further judgment upon the nation.

The Lord struck Egypt's greatest lifeline by turning the Nile River and all their waters into blood. The fish died and the water became completely useless for drinking. This plague proved that the river the Egyptians worshiped was entirely under God's control.

Frogs swarmed out of the waters and covered the entire land. They invaded common homes, food baskets, and even the private bedrooms of the royal palace. God showed that He did not need mighty armies to humble a proud and stubborn kingdom.

At God's command, swarms of flies and tiny gnats swept through every border of Egypt. These pests brought misery to both people and animals across the whole country. Even tiny insects obeyed the voice of the Creator to carry out His purpose.

A terrifying storm brought crushing hail and flashing lightning across Egypt, where heavy rain was almost unheard of. The storm shattered fruit trees, crushed grapevines, and ruined crops throughout the countryside. God stripped away the food and comfort the Egyptians relied on.

Huge swarms of locusts arrived at the Lord's word and darkened the sky. They devoured every green plant and crop left behind by the hail until the fields were completely bare. The natural world served as God's instrument to execute His judgment.

In the final plague, God struck down every firstborn son throughout Egypt, from the royal palace to the humblest home. The firstborn represented a family's hope and future strength. This heartbreaking loss finally broke Pharaoh's stubborn refusal to let the Israelites go.

The Lord brought Israel out enriched with silver and gold, given by the Egyptians as long-overdue pay for their years of slave labor. Even more remarkably, not a single person among the whole crowd was too weak or sick to travel. God gave His people complete strength for the long march ahead.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some modern prosperity and Word of Faith teachers claim this verse promises permanent physical health and wealth for all Christians today, rather than seeing it as a unique historical miracle for the Exodus.

notes.meaning: The Egyptians were glad to watch the Israelites leave their country. After enduring so many terrible disasters, the fear of Israel's God had fallen on everyone. They were eager to let them go just to save their own lives.

God spread a wide cloud over His people like a great tent to shield them from the scorching desert sun. At night, He gave them a pillar of fire to light their way and guard them in the dark. The Lord Himself watched over them by day and by night.

When the people needed food in the barren wilderness, God sent flocks of quail to provide meat. He also fed them with manna, a sweet flake that fell like bread from the sky every morning. The Lord graciously cared for their physical hunger in a dry and empty land.

When there was no water to drink, God split open a solid rock and fresh water gushed out. It flowed like a river across the dry ground, giving plenty to drink for the people and their herds. The Lord can bring life and refreshment out of the hardest places.

God did all these wonderful things because He remembered the holy promise He made to His servant Abraham long before. The people were delivered not because they were perfect, but because God is faithful to His word. His covenant love is the true source of every blessing.

The Lord led His chosen people on their journey with great joy and cheerful singing. After centuries of bitter oppression, they walked into freedom with shouts of victory. God turned their long season of mourning into a celebration of His goodness.

God brought Israel into the Promised Land and gave them cities, fields, and vineyards that other nations had built. They enjoyed the fruit of work they had not done, moving into homes they had not labored to build. Everything they possessed was an unearned gift of God's kindness.

God set His people free so that they would live holy lives, following His teachings and obeying His laws. Freedom was not given so they could do whatever they wanted, but so they could worship Him with loving hearts. The psalm ends with a joyful call for all people to praise the Lord.
